issues.display_title: Issue #194: Preview: metadata panel size resets when changing folder
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-20.at.13.56.02.mov

Problem

In Preview, the Images/metadata panel at the bottom can be resized (dragged taller). When the user navigates to a different folder, the panel snaps back to its default height instead of keeping the size the user set.

Root cause

src/renderer/features/preview/Preview.tsx:335 renders <Main /> only while files.displayedFile is set. Changing folder clears displayedFile, so Main unmounts and the react-resizable-panels Group (main-vertical) remounts with defaultSize again. The layout was never persisted.

Fix

Persist the vertical group layout with useDefaultLayout (built into react-resizable-panels v4, defaults to localStorage) and feed defaultLayout / onLayoutChanged back into the Group. panelIds follows showMetadata so the metadata-open and metadata-closed layouts are stored separately.

Files touched:

  • src/renderer/features/preview/Main.tsx

Acceptance criteria

  • Resize the metadata panel, switch folders, come back: the panel keeps the height the user set.
  • Same after an app restart.
  • Closing and reopening the metadata panel does not corrupt the main viewer layout.

Out of scope

Persisting the horizontal viewer/map split (main-viewer-inner) — separate task if needed.

issues.display_title: Issue #189: Duplicate freezes the window and never shows its progress modal
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-20.at.14.14.55.mov

What happens

Duplicating a multi-file selection freezes the window for the length of the copy, and the progress modal never appears — the copy itself finishes fine, but the app is unusable while it runs.

Two independent causes:

First, the UI thread. Every file the copy creates fires a watcher add, and each one made useBrowseFileEvents re-sort the entire folder and re-key every entry ({...item, sequence: index}), so every card in the grid re-rendered — once per duplicated file. Duplicating N files is O(N²) work on the renderer's main thread, which is what froze the window; the progress modal's state was being dispatched correctly all along, it just never got a frame to paint in.

Second, the native context menu's Duplicate did nothing at all. on_menu_event called the async msg_duplicate without awaiting or spawning it, so the future was dropped on the spot — no copy, and no duplicate progress events for the renderer's modal either. (The toolbar button never hit this; it goes through the command directly.)

The Rust side was already off the main thread — msg_duplicate runs its copy loop on spawn_blocking and emits duplicate processing/insert/success events per file.

How to reproduce

  1. Open a folder in Browse (Preview or Edit).
  2. Select a few dozen images.
  3. Toolbar → Duplicate (the clone icon).
  4. The window freezes until every copy lands; no progress modal shows.

Context-menu variant: right-click a selection → Duplicate → nothing happens at all.

Goal

Duplicating a large selection keeps the window responsive and shows the progress modal ticking from 0 to N, from both the toolbar and the right-click menu.

  • src-tauri/src/commands/context_menu.rs (on_menu_event) — spawn the msg_duplicate future instead of dropping it, matching the ChangeProjectType arm right below it. Context-menu Duplicate now actually copies and emits its progress events.
  • src/renderer/components/core/ipcHandlers/fileManager.ts (files-watcher) — coalesce a burst of watcher add/addDir entries into one setAddedFile dispatch (120ms window, deduped by path) instead of one dispatch per file. Collapses the O(N²) full-folder re-sort into a single pass per burst, so the UI thread stays free and the modal paints. Covers every bulk-create path — paste, batch export — not just duplicate.

Done on branch fix/loadfolder; pnpm typecheck + cargo check clean.

Follow-up (not in this change)

  • The grid is not virtualized: one re-render still touches every card. Worth doing if folders in the 2k+ range stay heavy after this.
  • One get-file-entry IPC round-trip per created file — batch it if the burst itself becomes the bottleneck.

issues.display_title: Issue #195: Image Info panel: minimize by dragging instead of hiding
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-20.at.14.49.46.mov

The Image Info (metadata) panel in the preview can be resized, but the 5px separator is invisible as an affordance and the panel cannot be swiped away: it stops at minSize and the only way to close it is the header X / the View-menu toggle, which unmounts it entirely so there is no way to bring it back by gesture.

Scope

  • Add a visible grip handle centered on the metadata separator so the drag target is discoverable.
  • Make the panel collapsible: dragging the grip down past the minimum collapses it to 0 instead of stopping.
  • Keep the separator + grip visible while collapsed, so it can be dragged back up. Never disappear entirely.
  • Header X becomes a minimize (chevron-down) that collapses the panel instead of hiding it.
  • E shortcut / View → Image Info toggles collapsed vs expanded, using the same state, so the menu check mark stays in sync.
  • Fix separator cursor: horizontal separators used col-resize; should be row-resize.
  • Do not persist a collapsed (0px) size to the stored layout — re-opening must restore a usable height.

Files

  • src/renderer/features/preview/Main.tsx — grip, collapsible panel, expand/collapse effect, resize→redux sync, layout-save guard
  • src/renderer/features/preview/Metadata.tsx — minimize button
  • src/renderer/index.css — row-resize cursor

Verification

pnpm typecheck clean; manual check of all three close paths (drag, minimize button, E) plus restoring by dragging the grip back up.

issues.display_title: Issue #186: Object Remover: one page for both flat photos and 360 panoramas
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-20.at.14.55.55.mov

Description

Problem: Object Remover is currently split into two separate entries in the Edit menu — one for regular photos and one for 360 panoramas. They look and behave exactly the same; the only real difference is which kind of photo they accept and which pipeline runs behind the scenes. Users have to know upfront which one to open, and picking the wrong one means the photo is rejected with a warning and they have to go back to the menu and start over.

Solution: One Object Remover entry that handles both. The app decides the variant from the photo itself: an image with an aspect ratio of 2:1 or wider is treated as a 360 panorama, anything else as a regular photo — the same rule the rest of the app already uses to detect panoramas. No toggle, no extra step for the user.

Behavior

  • Edit menu shows a single Object Remover item (the separate 360 entry goes away).
  • Drop or select any photo — regular or panorama, both are accepted.
  • The header shows a 360° chip once a panorama is loaded, so it is always visible which pipeline is running.
  • FAQ text, warnings, and the output folder follow the detected variant, exactly as they do today.
  • Removing objects, brush/box tools, save-as-new-file, and the before/after slider are unchanged.

Technical plan

The variant is derived from the image dimensions already in the store (state.files.fileDimensions) — no new state is added.

// features/objectRemover/constants.ts
export const variantFor = (dim?: ImageDimension) =>
  dim && isPano(dim) ? OBJECT_REMOVER_360 : OBJECT_REMOVER;

Content computes it once and passes it down through the variant prop that Preview, Settings, and useObjectRemover already take.

File Change
features/objectRemover/constants.ts add variantFor(); drop selectState / actions from the variant (single slice now)
features/edit/objectRemover/objectRemoverSlice.ts remove the second slice mount (objectRemover360Slice / Actions / Reducer)
features/edit/editReducer.ts remove the objectRemover360 branch
features/objectRemover/Content.tsx derive variant instead of receiving it as a prop
features/objectRemover/Preview.tsx accept both image kinds (dimensions must be readable); title + 360° chip
components/features/Edit/Menu.tsx remove the object-remover-360 entry
components/features/Edit/Edit.tsx remove the object-remover-360 case and the EditMenu union member
src/locales/*.json remove t_menu_edit.object-remover-360.*, update btn_description to cover flat + 360. t_object_remover_360.* (FAQ) stays

Backend is untouched — both generateObjectRemover and generateObjectRemover360 commands stay as they are.

Acceptance criteria

  • Only one Object Remover entry in the Edit menu.
  • A regular photo loads and runs the flat pipeline; output lands in Object remover.
  • A panorama loads in the same page and runs the 360 pipeline; output lands in 360 Object remover.
  • The 360° chip appears only for panoramas.
  • pnpm typecheck and pnpm i18n:check pass.

Known limitation

A flat photo that happens to be 2:1 or wider is detected as a panorama. Same rule the whole app uses today. If that turns out to bite real users, add a manual override toggle — not building it upfront.

issues.display_title: Issue #192: Scale Up Image fails on macOS: .exe-only binary lookup + output written relative to CWD
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Symptom

Every Scale Up Image job fails on macOS. Two separate defects, both invisible on Windows.

1. Upscaler binary is never found

run_one resolves the binary with a hardcoded Windows filename:

let Some(exe) = binary_path(app, "upscayl/upscayl-bin.exe") else {
    return RunResult::Failed("Upscaler binary not found".into());
};

The macOS binary is binaries/mac/upscayl/upscayl-bin (no extension), so binary_path returns None and every item fails with Upscaler binary not found.

Every other bundled tool already guards this (exiftool, enfuse, fisheye-stitch, nadir_overlay); scale_up.rs was the only one missing it.

2. Output is written relative to the process CWD

output_plan joins outputDirectory raw:

let target = Path::new(output_directory).join("Scale Up").join(name);

On non-Windows the renderer holds currentDirectory as a display-relative path anchored at $HOME or /Volumes (contract documented at src-tauri/src/commands/fs_ops.rs:535-538), e.g. Documents/Panorama. A relative join resolves against the process CWD, so the result landed inside the repo:

src-tauri/Documents/Panorama/Scale Up/gothru_capture_20260701_113324.jpg

Windows hides this because C:\... is already absolute.

Fix

  • Pick the binary name per platform via cfg!(windows).
  • Normalize outputDirectory through the existing files::normalize_target helper (the same one copy-sources uses) before building the plan. Absolute paths from openFolderDialog pass through unchanged.

Also found

output_plan's unit tests hardcoded C:\pics / D:\out literals and had been failing on any non-Windows host. Reworked to build fixtures from a platform-native base dir.

Verification

  • cargo test --lib scale_up → 5 passed
  • rustfmt --check src/commands/scale_up.rs → clean
  • upscayl-bin confirmed healthy standalone on macOS (universal Mach-O, no quarantine, exit 0 with the exact argv the command builds)

issues.display_title: Issue #187: Folder with uncached GPS positions blocks navigation until the sweep finishes
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-20.at.15.19.47.mov

Problem

Opening a folder with tens of thousands of panoramas whose GPS positions are not cached yet locks navigation: every way out of the folder — Back/Forward (mouse buttons 4/5), breadcrumbs, the path bar, reload, double-clicking another folder — is guarded by layout.onGettingGPSData and either does nothing or shows the "file is being validated" alert. The user is stuck watching the map spinner until the whole folder has been read, which on a network share is minutes.

Two things make it worse:

  1. The sweep cannot be cancelled. extract-gps-data reads every path in one par_iter pass and only writes to the gps table when the entire folder is done. Leaving the folder (once that were possible) would keep the disk/SMB reads running for a folder nobody is looking at.
  2. No resume. Because the cache write is all-or-nothing, an interrupted sweep leaves nothing behind — re-entering the folder starts from zero. And the renderer treats any cached row as "folder is fully cached" (if (cached.length) { publish; return; }), so a partial cache would be published as if it were complete.

Request

  • Back / navigation must work while the GPS sweep is running.
  • Leaving the folder stops the sweep.
  • Re-entering the folder continues from where it stopped instead of restarting.

Acceptance criteria

  • While GPS extraction runs, Back/Forward, breadcrumbs, path bar, reload and opening another folder all work normally (the onValidating guard stays; only the GPS guard goes).
  • Navigating away cancels the running extraction — no EXIF reads continue for the folder that was left.
  • Partial progress is cached, so re-entering the folder only reads the files that are still missing.
  • A late reply from a cancelled sweep never publishes its markers onto the folder that is open now.
  • The map spinner (DefaultMapCorner) still shows while a sweep is in progress.

Implementation

On development (working tree, not committed yet):

  • src-tauri/src/commands/metadata.rs — extract_gps_data now runs in chunks of 200 files; each chunk is written to the gps table as it lands, and a GPS_GENERATION counter is checked between chunks so a newer folder load stops the sweep. Same pattern as image::PREWARM_GENERATION. Adds cancel_gps_extract().
  • src-tauri/src/commands/files.rs — load-files calls cancel_gps_extract() next to the existing thumbnail prewarm cancel, so every navigation entry point cancels the sweep without a new IPC channel.
  • src/renderer/features/preview/hooks/usePreviewGPSData.ts — diffs the cached rows against the folder's images and asks Rust only for the missing paths (this is the resume), publishes the cached subset immediately, and guards the late reply with the requested directory.
  • Removed the onGettingGPSData guard from the 8 navigation call sites (preview/Browse.tsx, fileManager/Browse.tsx, Edit/Browse.tsx, PathBar.tsx, PanelBreadcrumbs.tsx, MessageModal.tsx, preview/Preview.tsx mouse back/forward). onValidating is untouched.

Not covered

Real progress reporting. The indicator still jumps 0% → 100%; showing per-chunk progress needs a progress event from Rust to the renderer. Worth a follow-up if the spinner looks hung on very large folders.

issues.display_title: Issue #188: perf: grid lag + 100% disk usage on folders with tens of thousands of images
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-20.at.15.19.47.mov

What happens

Opening a folder with tens of thousands of images makes the browse grid stutter while scrolling, and disk usage stays at 100% for minutes after scrolling stops.

Cause: every ImageItem fires get-thumb the moment its card mounts. Fast scrolling mounts and unmounts thousands of cards; the renderer cancels its own promise on unmount but the backend does not, so each stale request still queues a full-file decode behind thumb_semaphore. Scrolling past 10k images enqueues ~10k decodes for thumbnails nobody is looking at any more — the disk reads whole source files (a 32MP panorama in full, per decode), and the thumbnails actually on screen wait behind that backlog. get_thumb made it worse by acquiring a semaphore permit before checking the cache, so even a cache hit queued.

Second, independent load: the GPS sweep (extract_gps_data) reads EXIF for every image in the folder via par_iter. Chunked and cancellable, but unbounded — a 30k-panorama folder is minutes of sustained I/O right after the folder opens, competing with thumbnail decodes.

How to reproduce

  1. Open a folder with 10k+ images (Preview or File Manager).
  2. Scroll fast to the bottom and back.
  3. Scroll stutters; disk usage stays at 100% long after scrolling stops.

Goal

Scrolling a 10k+ image folder stays smooth, and disk I/O settles shortly after the user stops scrolling — no work left running for thumbnails already scrolled past.

  • src/renderer/features/preview/ImageItem.tsx — request the thumbnail only after the card stays mounted ~150ms, so cards that fly past never hit IPC. Shared component: covers Preview / Edit / File Manager grids.
  • src-tauri/src/commands/image.rs (get_thumb) — check the thumbnail cache (one stat) before acquiring a semaphore permit, so a cache hit returns immediately instead of queueing behind in-flight decodes.
  • src-tauri/src/commands/metadata.rs (extract_gps_data) — throttled instead of capped: coordinates are only known after the EXIF read, so a viewport-driven sweep is impossible for uncached files, and a hard cap would leave a big folder's map showing partial markers with no signal which are missing. The sweep now waits 1.5s before its first read (thumbnails on screen get the disk first, and leaving during the delay costs nothing) and reads on a dedicated 4-thread rayon pool instead of the global one, so it no longer takes every core off the thumbnail decodes. Markers stay complete.
  • src-tauri/src/commands/image.rs (get_thumb) — a queued request captures PREWARM_GENERATION (bumped on every folder load) before waiting for its semaphore permit and drops itself if the generation moved while it waited, so navigating away no longer leaves the previous folder's decodes running. Returns "" for a dropped request; ImageItem retries once after 400ms so a same-folder reload (card still mounted, effect never re-runs) can't leave a permanent placeholder. Scroll-past inside one folder is still handled by the 150ms settle delay — the two cover different cases.

Done on branch fix/loadfolder; pnpm typecheck + cargo check clean (the 2 cargo clippy errors in nadir.rs / pano_level are pre-existing and untouched).

issues.display_title: Issue #197: macOS stitching fails: pto_gen --sort on Hugin 2019.2, then the image-crate 512 MiB limit
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Symptom

On macOS every stitch job fails at step 1/8 with:

Error: Step 1/8 (Generating project file) failed:
.../src-tauri/target/debug/binaries/mac/fisheye-stitch/models/pto_gen exited with Some(1)
--- stderr ---
pto_gen: unrecognized option `--sort'

Windows is unaffected by this first failure. Reproduced with 8 circular-fisheye
photos (2 panoramas, 4 frames each).

Root cause

Two independent bugs, the second only visible once the first is out of the way.
Both live in the fisheye-stitch source (GoThruMedia/fisheye-stitch), not in
this repo — this repo only vendors the built binary.

1. pto_gen --sort does not exist in the macOS Hugin build

src/pipeline.rs passed --sort to pto_gen unconditionally. The flag landed
in Hugin 2020.0; the tools bundled in src-tauri/binaries/mac/fisheye-stitch/models/
are 2019.2.0 (built by Niklas Mischkulnig, x86_64-only), where pto_gen
exits 1 on it. The Windows bundle is newer and documents the flag, hence the
platform split.

Upgrading the macOS Hugin bundle is not an option right now: 2019.2 is also what
the current Hugin.app for macOS ships (verified against /Applications/Hugin),
so the flag had to go instead. --sort only orders the inputs alphanumerically,
and fisheye-stitch already hands the images over in filename order — the source
comment right below the call said as much.

Also checked, since the same version gap could hide more of these: every other
flag the pipeline passes (cpfind --prealigned/--multirow/--sieve2size/--ransacmode rpy/--ransacdist/--fullscale, pano_modify --canvas=AUTO, enblend --blend-colorspace=identity, nona -m TIFF_m -z) is accepted by the 2019.2 tools.

2. image::open refuses panoramas over 512 MiB

With --sort gone the pipeline ran 1/8 → 8/8 and then failed at the final
conversion:

Error: Could not decode enblend's TIFF output with the `image` crate, and no
ImageMagick (`magick`) binary was found on PATH to fall back to.

enblend writes an uncompressed 8-bit RGBA TIFF (verified with exiftool:
Compression: Uncompressed, SamplesPerPixel: 4, RowsPerStrip: 14), which
image supports fine — the blocker is size. At 17702x8458 that buffer is 570 MiB,
past the 512 MiB max_alloc that image 0.25 applies by default. Decoding the
captured TIFF with a standalone image 0.25 binary confirms it:

ERR Limits(LimitError { kind: InsufficientMemory })

The ImageMagick fallback then can't save it, because magick is bundled on
neither platform. This one is not macOS-specific — any panorama over the
limit fails the same way on Windows unless the user happens to have ImageMagick
on PATH, which is the likely reason it went unnoticed there.

Fix

In GoThruMedia/fisheye-stitch, src/pipeline.rs (patched locally, not yet
committed/pushed):

  • drop --sort, pass images directly (already in filename order)
  • read the enblend TIFF through ImageReader + no_limits() instead of
    image::open; the ImageMagick fallback stays for genuinely unsupported TIFF
    variants

In this repo: src-tauri/binaries/mac/fisheye-stitch/fisheye-stitch replaced
with a universal (x86_64 + arm64) rebuild, ad-hoc signed. tauri dev picks it
up automatically — target/debug/binaries mirrors the source tree.

Verification

Both panoramas from the reported folder now run 8/8 to a finished file, using
the vendored binary in place:

  • 01–04.jpg → 17702x8851 JPEG, 22.7 MB
  • 05–08.jpg → 17702x8851 JPEG, 25.2 MB

Output checked visually: valid equirectangular, seams closed, nadir hole only
where the shoot has no bottom frame.

Remaining work

  • Commit + push the fisheye-stitch src/pipeline.rs patch upstream
  • Rebuild the Windows binary with the same patch and re-vendor
    src-tauri/binaries/win/fisheye-stitch/fisheye-stitch.exe — it still
    carries bug 2, so large panoramas fail there without ImageMagick on PATH.
    Needs an MSVC host; not cross-buildable from this mac.
  • Re-run a stitch on Windows after that to confirm parity

Issue #198: Stitching: fix progress bar glitches and control-points editor bug
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Video.Project.18.mp4

Summary

Bundle of Stitching fixes.

  • Progress bar no longer jumps backward. When the stitching engine retries matching points between photos, the progress bar used to visibly rewind (both on each panorama's card and the overall queue bar). Now it only moves forward.
  • Progress no longer resets when switching pages. Leaving the Stitching page mid-run and coming back used to show 0% again even though the job kept running in the background. It now shows the real, current progress.
  • Cleaned up the progress display. Removed the confusing "X minutes left" text above the queue progress bar.
  • Fixed the manual control-points editor breaking after a failed match. If the engine couldn't find any matching points for a panorama, opening "Manual control points" showed nothing to work with, and the next attempt couldn't be saved either. It now starts from a clean slate instead.
  • Updated the stitching engine binary, including a macOS compatibility fix.

Why it matters

These issues made stitching jobs that were actually running fine look broken or stuck, and could leave users unable to manually fix a panorama that failed automatic matching.
